summary: SL-042 moved the counting rule into ScanStore. Append now does first-seen dedup and posts each charged file up the Parent chain into three new per-row columns (RolledSize, RolledOnDisk, FilesBelow). The new ScanStore.Rollup.cs adds ChildrenLargestFirst, which sorts on every read. The Scanner's own copies of the rule are gone, and its totals go through one Credit helper. Build, code review and validate each passed on the first attempt (188/188 tests, real scans of C:\Windows and C:\Program Files). All the rework was upstream: 29 design attempts (27 wasted on a provider session limit), two halts waved through, and 13 critique findings, of which 10 were accepted.

The new ScanStore.Rollup.cs adds ChildrenLargestFirst, which sorts on every read. The Scanner's own copies of the rule are gone, and its totals go through one Credit helper. Build, code review and validate each passed on the first attempt (188/188 tests, real scans of C:\Windows and C:\Program Files). All the rework was upstream: 29 design attempts (27 wasted on a provider session limit), two halts waved through, and 13 critique findings, of which 10 were accepted.

learned.lesson: In this loop the critic reasons from the design text and the web. It does not open the repo. The step that opened the repo was the disposition of its findings. That step refuted four of the critic's claims about existing code and corrected two accepted findings. Before accepting any critique claim about an existing test, rule or reader, check it against the file it names.
learned.evidence: M4 gave the wrong threshold (private bytes against 1 GiB); the real test measures a GC-heap delta against 800 MiB and already sits in a DisableParallelization collection (ScanStoreTests.cs:109-117). m5 and m6 were refuted by eng/rules-harness/plants.json F03, xunit 2.9.3 in the csproj, and the existing CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped rule. M-add-1 guessed at an App reader that does not exist (grep found only TopLevelTracker.cs:61-62). m3's fix, throwing on mark-Unreadable when ChildCount > 0, would have thrown on every partial listing, because DirectoryReader.List keeps entries read before an error (DirectoryReader.cs:86-89).

learned.lesson: Project facts that stop repeat false positives. `**/` in an architecture-rule glob matches zero directory levels, so a plant such as F03 fires on files directly in the folder. The test project is on xUnit v2, where there is no Explicit. `\bExplicit\s*=\s*true` is already forbidden across tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/**. A settled architecture rule without including_comments matches code only, so a comment naming Scanner in the store cannot trip it.
learned.evidence: Dispositions of m5 and m6 cite eng/rules-harness/plants.json:8, fitness.yaml:57-60 and 135, ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:82, and FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj:15.

learned.lesson: The Scanner writes to store rows after appending them, at two sites: the first holder's row when a repeated ID is found, and the entry itself. Both go through the store's unconditional CorrectSizes(index, ...), which posts the change in the charge up that row's own Parent chain. Append and CorrectSizes both return Posted(Size, OnDisk, Files), and Scanner.Credit(entry, posted, inPlace) is the only feeder of Totals and TopLevelTracker. inPlace exists because the tracker credits Append postings at FolderDone but credits corrections immediately. Any later slice that touches counting in Scanner.cs must keep that single feeder and run Scans.AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals.
learned.evidence: M1 disposition cites Scanner.cs:235-247 and 253-254. Build deviation: Credit gained inPlace. The mutant 'correction not posted' failed HardlinkTests (2,1), (3,2) and TopLevelTests.AnInPlaceCorrection.

learned.lesson: For a slice that moves a rule out of one component, the survey and the design must list every writer of the affected columns, not just the block being deleted. The design here said nothing needed the first holder's index and that one grep would settle the probe question. Both were wrong, and only the critic caught it.
learned.evidence: build-check named Scanner.cs:235-249 as the dedup site and did not list the post-append correction writers; critique finding M1 was confirmed by the repo.

learned.lesson: ScanStoreBudgetTests is a GC-heap delta against 800 MiB, not process private bytes. It used to chain every folder under the previous one, about 500,000 deep, so any posting-at-append design multiplies the work by depth (about 10^12 adds). It now nests at most 16 deep, with one 100,000-child folder. With the three rollup columns, retained memory went from 555.8 to 652.1 MiB (+96 MiB), with a peak of 678.4 MiB in validate, so about 122 MiB of headroom remains against 800 MiB. The pre-decided fallback is a folder-slot layout (about 30 MiB instead of 95 MiB). Gate the next per-row column on this test, and measure private bytes on the real store, which nobody has done.
learned.evidence: M4 disposition (ScanStoreTests.cs:109-117 and 145); build and validate memory numbers; the spike measured only a throwaway 51 B/row layout at 887.8 MiB.

learned.lesson: Nothing at run time enforces the single-writer, deterministic-order invariant behind 'first name charges'. The M3 guard was rightly overridden, because a lock or flag cannot see nondeterministic order. Root-equals-Totals assertions cannot detect the failure either, because the root is conserved and only the per-folder split moves. Validate showed repeatability only for today's single-threaded Scanner (3 scans of C:\Windows, 0 of 157,748 folders moved). Any slice that parallelises listing must either serialise appends deterministically or re-agree criterion 2 as per-subtree counting. Its check must compare per-folder totals across runs, not the root.
learned.evidence: Spike first-seen-charging-repeatable: with 16 workers, 68 folders moved more than 10 MiB (WinSxS 587 MiB) while the control moved 0 B and the root stayed at 41,044,790,312 bytes. Validate's repeat probe. M3's override reason.

learned.lesson: A design stage where every designer fails on the provider's session limit is not classified as a provider halt. The first attempt was recognised, but 27 of the next 28 recorded 'no designer returned a usable proposal' with no caused_by and were retried for about 2.5 hours. Check that the restart-after-'not now' logic (07d3627) keys off the provider's text (session limit, reset time), not off a stage-level 'no usable proposal' outcome.
learned.evidence: design-slice #1 message 'You've hit your session limit · resets 10:50pm (Asia/Kolkata)'. The build-slice account records 29 attempts, 27 with no caused_by and no changes. Commit 00cf7df says two parallel slices tripped the limit in two hours.

learned.lesson: Two early gates halt on states that are expected for this kind of slice, and each halt was waved through. build-check returns 'partial' with four criteria missing when the slice's job is to create them. risk-spike returned a no-go on a 16-worker method the design never used, though the finding did become the single-writer invariant. Budget a halt round for each on a store or scanner slice, and read the halt text before treating it as a blocker.
learned.evidence: build-check #1 halted then #2 'built anyway despite a partial survey'; risk-spike #1 halted then #2 'built anyway despite a no-go spike'.

learned.lesson: Mutation scripting trap in this repo: restoring a source with Copy-Item keeps the backup's older timestamp, so MSBuild skips the rebuild and the last mutant's DLL stays in bin. Touch the source or use --no-incremental after every restore, or the next full run fails for no reason. Separately, the first Release build in a fresh worktree downloads the .NET 10 SDK (about 300 MB) into .dotnet/, because the machine has only SDKs 8 and 9.
learned.evidence: build-slice check row: 7 failed, 181 passed after the mutation script, source hash-identical, passing after touch and rebuild. build-check installed SDK 10.0.401.

learned.lesson: On this store and scanner code the defects were found at critique, not at the back-end gates. The two real majors (M1, M2) were both mutation-verified as load-bearing. Code-review and validate found no defect. Validate's only failed line is a check of leaf fidelity, not of this slice: file-level on-disk sizes differ from the handle route in WinSxS\Manifests (15,048 B) and one powershell.common folder (3,632 B). A later validator should expect that difference and not chase it as a regression.
learned.evidence: code-review #1 and validate #1 passed first time; the mutation list; validate's [failed] oracle B, called pre-existing and file-level outside C1-C6.

candidates.title: Semantic merge check between SL-040 and SL-042 before either merges
candidates.why: Both branches edit ScanStore.cs and commit-slice resolves no conflicts. SL-042 makes TryAddFileId private, makes Append clear a caller-supplied HardlinkDuplicate, and makes AddFlags throw on it. Any SL-040 test that builds a duplicate by hand will fail to compile or start charging. Nobody could see SL-040's tests during critique or validate (validate: not-run).

candidates.title: Edit the recorded Scan Store architecture line to sort-on-read, and close the sort-on-read question on the measured numbers
candidates.why: The m9 obligation was discharged by writing the revised line into docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md. The engine's recorded line still says children are stored sorted largest first, which is what the next slice reads. The 100,000-child read measured 9-40 ms against 250 ms, so the evidence to decide exists.

candidates.title: Tree slice: read ChildrenLargestFirst in the window, measure the screen's half of the 0.5 s budget, and retire TopLevelTracker with the SL-039 'window never touches the scan store' rule
candidates.why: Nothing in the window reads ChildrenLargestFirst yet (validate: not reached). TopLevelTracker is now a second accumulator of numbers the store owns, held equal only by real-tree assertions. The build says the tree slice can delete it and the rule on purpose.

candidates.title: Measure process private bytes on a full C:\ scan with the rollup columns in the real ScanStore
candidates.why: Validate scanned only C:\Windows (346,280 entries) and C:\Program Files (87,862). The budget test is a GC-heap delta (652.1 MiB retained, 678.4 MiB peak against 800 MiB). The spike's 1 GiB private-bytes verdict was on a throwaway layout with about 136 MiB of headroom, and this slice spent 96 MiB of retained memory.

candidates.title: Fix the window's counters lagging the final totals at the end of a scan
candidates.why: Seen on the trunk exe as well: on C:\Windows CountersText read 184,376 files against a final 188,532, while OutcomeDetail showed the final figures. It is a user-visible wrong number, not changed by this slice.

candidates.title: Engine: treat a design stage where every designer fails on the provider's session limit as a provider halt, not a retry
candidates.why: 27 of 29 design attempts on this slice recorded 'no designer returned a usable proposal' with no caused_by, over about 2.5 hours. Confirm whether 07d3627 covers this classification.

candidates.title: Explain the file-level on-disk differences between the listing and the handle route (WinSxS\Manifests 15,048 B, a powershell.common folder 3,632 B)
candidates.why: Seen only in validate's handle-route oracle, under the Scanner's 64 MiB no-probe threshold. It is pre-existing and outside C1-C6, and validate did not identify which files cause it. It bears on the epic's 'each file's current size' promise.

candidates.title: Engine: do not halt build-check on 'partial' when the only gaps are the slice's own criteria
candidates.why: build-check #1 halted with four of six criteria missing and two partial, which is the expected state for a slice that builds them. It was waved through on the next call, costing a halt round.

payload.estimate_error: The size (medium) and tier (high) were right for the work, and the tier was earned. The build needed one attempt (8 files, 18 new tests plus migrated ones, 188/188), and critique majors M1 (post-append correction of the first holder's row) and M2 (all-ones ID sentinel) would each have silently lost bytes. Their mutants fail tests. But the risk was concentrated in critique: code-review and validate found no defect. The schedule error was not about size. About 2.5 hours went to 27 design retries against a provider session limit, and two early halts (build-check, risk-spike) each cost a round for a state the slice was built to change.

missed.what: The critique filed M4 about the 5M-entry budget test but did not read how the test builds its tree. The test chains every folder under the previous one (folder = store.Append(folder, ...)), about 500,000 deep. Posting each file up the Parent chain at append time would then cost about 10^12 ancestor adds, and the design's '60M adds at realistic depth' and 'must pass unchanged' both ignored it. A check would have been: what depth does each existing test feed the append path?
missed.caught_by: M4's disposition (the model triage that opened ScanStoreTests.cs), before build. The critic's own M4 was about parallel-test contention and used the wrong threshold.

missed.what: The design made the store the only source of HardlinkDuplicate but guarded only Append (private TryAddFileId, plus a rule matching `|= EntryFlags.HardlinkDuplicate`). The Scanner also set the flag through AddFlags(entry, HardlinkDuplicate), which neither the rule nor the private method covers. The critic did not ask what other paths can set the flag.
missed.caught_by: build-slice, which made AddFlags throw on HardlinkDuplicate (declared deviation).

missed.what: The m2 fix (route Totals and TopLevelTracker through one Credit(entry, delta) helper) missed that TopLevelTracker is credited at FolderDone for Append postings but immediately for in-place corrections. The helper needed an inPlace flag, and the critic did not read TopLevelTracker.cs to see it.

The review of the critique called 'all nine minors valid at minor', but m5 (rule globs vacuous, comments could trip the rule) and m6 (xUnit v3 Explicit) were both false. plants.json F03 shows `**/` matches zero levels, the project is on xUnit 2.9.3, and an existing rule already forbids Explicit. It also called M4 'one attribute' when the test already sat in a non-parallel collection and had a real depth problem. It did not open plants.json, fitness.yaml or the csproj.
missed.caught_by: The disposition step, which overrode m5 and m6 after reading eng/rules-harness/plants.json, fitness.yaml and FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj.

missed.what: The gap it added (M-add-1, unseen readers of a folder row's ChargedSize) named a reader that does not exist. It guessed at App and --report readers without grepping src/. Its verification cost a disposition round.
missed.caught_by: M-add-1's disposition: a grep of src/ found only TopLevelTracker.cs:61-62, and the App uses the store only via GetPath.

unknowns: Does a folder's own directory allocation matter on any volume that reports it? Local NTFS lists every folder at EndOfFile 0 and AllocationSize 0 (356 folders probed), so dropping folders' own sizes from Totals is a no-op locally. Whether an SMB-LOOPBACK rig, which lists 4096 intermittently, changes the answer is unmeasured, and the real-NTFS half of C-008 was never built.

When listing is parallelised (U-012 makes it likely), should appends be serialised deterministically or should criterion 2 be re-agreed as per-subtree counting? The second lets children sum to more than their parent. Nothing enforces the single-writer order at run time.

What is the process private-bytes peak of the real ScanStore with rollup columns at 5M entries or on a full C:\ scan (about 2.4M files)? Only the GC-heap figure (652.1 retained, 678.4 peak) exists, against an 800 MiB budget.

Does sort-on-read hold once the screen adds its own cost? ChildrenLargestFirst measured 9-40 ms at 100,000 children, but nothing in the window calls it yet, so the 0.5 s tree budget's screen half is unmeasured.

Which files cause the file-level on-disk differences (15,048 B in WinSxS\Manifests, 3,632 B in a powershell.common folder) between listing sizes and handle-route sizes below the 64 MiB probe threshold?
what_went_wrong: design-slice ran 29 attempts. 27 ended as 'no designer returned a usable proposal' from the provider's session limit, with no caused_by, over about 2.5 hours. Only the first was classified as a provider halt. Commit 00cf7df shows two parallel slices caused the limit.

build-check halted on a 'partial' verdict, though the slice exists to build the missing criteria. risk-spike halted on a no-go for a 16-worker method the design never used. Each was waved through on the next call, so each cost a halt round.

The designer wrote that nothing needs the first holder's index and that one grep would settle the probe question. That was wrong: the Scanner corrects the first holder's row after append. The build-check survey had listed the dedup lines but not the post-append correction writers, so only the critic caught it (M1).

The design said the 5M-entry budget test 'must pass unchanged' without opening it. The test builds a chain about 500,000 deep, which incremental posting would turn into about 10^12 adds. Only M4's disposition noticed, and the critic and the review of the critic both missed it.

The critic made four wrong or misdirected claims about existing code (M4's threshold, m5, m6, M-add-1) and one accepted finding came with a fix that would have thrown on every partial listing (m3). The critique-review endorsed two of the wrong ones as valid. The disposition step, not the two review gates, did the checking against the repo.

The m9 obligation is marked discharged, but the fix landed only in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md. The recorded architecture line the next slice reads still says children are stored sorted. The finding's own reason for existing is unmet.

The build's mutation script restored sources with Copy-Item, which kept the old timestamp, so MSBuild skipped the rebuild. The first full run then failed 7 tests on a stale DLL and needed a touch, rebuild and rerun.

The real-NTFS half of case C-008 was never built, because local NTFS lists folders at 0/0. The synthetic 4096/4096 case stands in for it. O-008 is marked discharged on that basis, so the folder-owns-an-allocation case has not run against anything real.
